import datetime
import calendar


def next_billing_date(start: datetime.date, months_ahead: int) -> datetime.date:
    """Return the billing date ``months_ahead`` months after ``start``.

    The day-of-month is preserved.  When the target month is shorter than
    ``start.day`` (e.g. Jan 31 + 1 month), the result is clamped to the
    last day of the target month — the standard convention for billing
    cycles.

    ``months_ahead`` may be zero (returns ``start``) or negative (goes
    backward in time).
    """
    # Convert to a flat month index, shift, then convert back.
    # Python's floor-division and modulo handle negative offsets correctly.
    total_months = start.year * 12 + (start.month - 1) + months_ahead
    target_year, month_zero = divmod(total_months, 12)
    target_month = month_zero + 1

    # Clamp the day to the last valid day of the target month.
    max_day = calendar.monthrange(target_year, target_month)[1]
    target_day = min(start.day, max_day)

    return datetime.date(target_year, target_month, target_day)
